# Gym Log
Running log of gym sessions (strength work not captured by Strava). Most recent first.
---
## 23 Aug 2026 (evening) — light taper upper body, 8 days out from Sydney
**Context:** Deliberately light session per taper plan — no failure sets, no new loaded movements, moderate weights only.
- **Shoulder press (DB):** 14kg × 12 × 3 sets
- **Dumbbell bench press:** 16kg × 12 × 3 sets
- **Single-arm DB row:** 20kg × 12 × 3 sets
- **Dead hangs (added, not in plan):** 10s × 3 — reported as easy
**Strava data** ("Evening Weight Training", id 19869826107): 54 min duration · 197 kcal · avg HR 80 bpm · max HR 110 bpm
**Coach review:**
- Lowest HR of any session logged so far (avg 80, max 110) — genuinely confirms this was a light, easy day, exactly as intended for taper week.
- Session followed the plan closely on the three main movements — good discipline holding back on load 8 days from race.
- Dead hangs were added despite being flagged to skip grip work today. Low actual cost (10s × 3, reported as easy) so no real harm — but worth naming as the same instinct that showed up on Aug 19 (extending sessions past what was planned). Not a concern in isolation, but worth staying aware of this close to race day, when the value of "add a bit more" is low and the downside of any irritation is high.
- **Recovery:** Minimal session load. Nothing here should affect the rest of taper week or the flight Wednesday.
---
## 19 Aug 2026 (afternoon) — leg day, 11 days out from Sydney
**Context:** Leg day continuing squat/deadlift progression. First trial of light isometric calf/Achilles holds since the tendinopathy began. Race-proximity discipline applied throughout — moderate loads, no max singles, one new low-risk grip movement added, new loaded leg patterns deliberately avoided this close to race day.
- **Squats:** 12×bar (warm-up) → 12×70kg → 10×80kg → 8×90kg (planned 6, ran 8 — slight volume creep)
- **Lateral squats (superset w/ squats):** 3×12×15kg (up from 12.5kg last session — real load increase on a stability exercise this close to race)
- **Deadlift:** 12×60kg → 8×80kg → 4×80kg (capped third set deliberately, avoiding repeat grip failure pattern from Aug 8/12)
- **Barbell row / calf isometric hold superset:**
- Set 1: Row 12×40kg / Calf hold 25s
- Set 2: Row 12×50kg / Calf hold 25s
- Set 3: Row 10×50kg / Calf hold 25s
- Row exceeded the 42.5kg target, reaching 50kg — strong progress on the flagged laggard lift
- **Calf holds: felt fine throughout, no pain or pulling.** Clean first trial.
- **Farmer's carries (NEW movement):** 3×20m @ 28kg/hand, shoes on. Challenging but controlled — good baseline for a first session.
**Strava data** ("Afternoon Weight Training", id 19814349740): 98 min duration · 467 kcal · avg HR 98 bpm · max HR 147 bpm
**Coach review:**
- Calf isometric trial went cleanly — felt fine through all three 25s holds. This is the key result of the session; the fuller signal is tomorrow morning's first-steps check, but a clean same-day report is a good start toward reintroducing calf work.
- Squats ran hotter than planned (8 reps vs planned 6 at 90kg) and lateral squats jumped load (12.5→15kg) — neither is dangerous alone, but flagged as load creep worth watching given the taper window; the discipline point here isn't the numbers themselves; it's noticing the pattern of extending sessions past plan on a good-feeling day.
- Deadlift capping at a 4-rep third set (rather than repeating a full 8) was a good disciplined call — avoided re-testing grip failure this close to race, banked a bit more volume without the risk.
- Barbell row hit 50kg (target was 42.5kg) — genuinely good progress on the previously lagging lift.
- Farmer's carries added as a new, low-risk grip-specific movement — appropriate choice for this point in the taper (unlike a new loaded leg pattern, which was deliberately avoided given race proximity). Good first data point (28kg/hand, 20m, "felt it") to build from post-race.
- **Recovery:** Solid volume day. Tomorrow morning's Achilles check is the most important data point from today's entire session — that determines whether calf work continues to progress through the rest of the taper.

## 14 Aug 2026 (flat gym, chiller session)
**Context:** Mobility warm-up. At flat gym (not usual Hiit.io gym), so some equipment substitutions and no cycle to/from. Two days after 12 Aug leg day — complementary upper-body, deliberately lower intensity.
- **Shoulder press (DB):** 14kg × 12 × 3 sets
- **Dumbbell bench press:** 18kg × 12 × 3 sets (last set a genuine grind, only just hit 12)
- **Triceps pushdown:** 10×18.1kg (too hard, dropped weight) → 12×13.6kg (clean)
- **Single-arm DB row / dead hang superset** (substitute — no row/lat pulldown machine at this gym):
- Set 1: Row 20kg×12 / Dead hang 10s
- Set 2: Row 20kg×12 / Dead hang 10s
- Set 3: Row 20kg×12 / Dead hang 10s
**Strava data** ("Evening Weight Training", id 19742469798, no cycle — flat gym session): 64 min duration · 262 kcal · avg HR 84 bpm · max HR 122 bpm
**Coach review:**
- Good self-regulation — dropping triceps pushdown weight after 18.1kg proved too hard for 10 reps was the right call rather than grinding an accessory lift.
- DB bench at 18kg/side: last set only just landed 12 reps — that's genuine current capacity. Same lesson as squats: don't jump straight past this next time, use a small bridging step (e.g. 20kg) rather than a big jump.
- Nice equipment adaptation — swapped to single-arm DB rows when this gym lacked a row/pulldown machine, keeping pulling volume in rather than skipping it.
- Folding dead hangs into the row sets as a superset was a smart way to add grip work (flagged after Aug 12's grip-limited deadlifts) without needing a separate block.
- HR data confirms this was genuinely the chiller session intended — lowest avg (84) and max (122) HR of any session logged so far, well below Aug 8/9/12.
**Recovery:** Low-strain session overall. Shoulders did real work today (press + bench + rows all load the shoulder girdle) — if anything's sore tomorrow it's more likely shoulders than legs. Shouldn't interfere with running.

## 8 Aug 2026
**Context:** Cycled to gym, mobility warm-up, cycled home. Achilles: no pain during or after.
- **Squats:** 12×bar (warm-up) → 12×60kg → 10×80kg → 8×90kg → 2×100kg
- **Lateral squats (superset w/ squats):** 12×bodyweight → 12×10kg
- **Deadlift:** 12×60kg → 8×80kg → 8×80kg
- **Bench press:** 12×bar (warm-up) → 10×40kg → 10×40kg → 8×50kg
- **Barbell row:** 3×40kg
- Stretch to finish
**Strava data** ("Morning Weight Training", id 19653696465): 87 min duration · 523 kcal · avg HR 112 bpm · max HR 158 bpm
**Notes:** First 100kg squat single logged. Achilles handled squat/deadlift loading with no issues. Max HR of 158 likely corresponds to the top squat single.
**Coach review:**
- Squat jump from 8×90kg to 2×100kg was large — a bridging set (~4-5×95kg) would give cleaner progression data next time.
- Barbell row (3×40kg) remains the most under-loaded lift relative to squat/deadlift progression — worth a small deliberate nudge (extra rep or +2.5kg) every few sessions.
- Lateral squat superset is a good addition for ankle/Achilles stability work.
- No direct calf/Achilles strengthening this session (consistent with the long-term gap identified). Reintroduce controlled isometric calf holds (not deep stretch) once ankle stability is confirmed over a few more sessions.
- **Recovery:** Treat the next day as genuinely easy — legs took real volume today. Morning-after stiffness/pain on first steps is the key Achilles signal to watch, more than in-session feel.

## 9 Aug 2026 (evening)
**Context:** Cycled to gym (cycle included in this Strava session), standard mobility warm-up (child's pose side-to-side, cat-cow, hip mobility + fire hydrants, scorpions, 90/90s, lunge with back stretch, ankle mobility toe/heel walking, core, other bits). Complementary upper-body session to 8 Aug's leg day — no lower body loading, Achilles given a clean day.
- **Shoulder press / bicep curl superset:**
- Set 1: Shoulder press 12×12.5kg (DB) / Bicep curl 12×bar
- Set 2: Shoulder press 12×12.5kg (DB) / Barbell curl 12×(bar+2.5kg/side)
- Set 3: Shoulder press 12×15kg (DB) / Barbell curl 12×(bar+5kg/side)
- **Incline chest press / triceps pushdown superset:**
- Set 1: Incline press 12×15kg (DB) / Pushdown 12×18.1kg
- Set 2: Incline press 12×15kg (DB) / Pushdown 10×18.1kg
- Set 3: Incline press 12×15kg (DB), near-failure / Pushdown 8×18.1kg
- **Seated row / lat pulldown superset:**
- Set 1: Seated row 8×36kg / Lat pulldown 8×36kg
- Set 2: Seated row 8×36kg / Lat pulldown 8×36kg
- Set 3: Seated row 8×36kg / Lat pulldown 8×36kg
**Strava data** ("Afternoon Weight Training", id 19671739521, includes cycle to/from gym): 67 min duration · 304 kcal · avg HR 102 bpm · max HR 133 bpm
**Coach review:**
- Good complementary session to leg day — upper push/pull + arms, no lower body loading.
- Shoulder press and barbell curl both progressed in load across sets.
- Triceps pushdown reps dropped set to set (12→10→8) while incline press held steady at 12 — triceps fatigued faster than chest in the superset. Consider sequencing pushdown first, or trimming pushdown weight slightly to better match volume across the pair.
- Rows/pulldowns held steady at 8×36kg across all 3 sets with no drop-off — room to add load next time.
- **Recovery:** normal upper-body session load — standard protein/sleep, shouldn't affect tomorrow's running unless arms/shoulders are unusually sore.

## 12 Aug 2026 (evening)
**Context:** 35 min cycle to gym, 10 min mobility warm-up. Leg day continuing the squat/deadlift progression thread — plan built to fix the Aug 8 note about the 90→100kg squat jump being too large to read progression cleanly.
- **Squats:** 12×bar (warm-up) → 12×65kg → 10×80kg → 8×90kg → 5×95kg (bridging set, difficult, ~1-2 reps in reserve) → **1×100kg** (clean form, reps left in the tank, stopped deliberately)
- **Lateral squats (superset w/ squats):** 12×10kg → 12×12.5kg → 12×12.5kg → 12×12.5kg (hit today's 12.5kg target early, held steady)
- **Deadlift:** 8×60kg (felt tired; grip was the limiter, not legs) → 8×80kg (no straps, grip loosening but held) → 8×80kg (held rather than nudging to 85kg, since grip was already the constraint)
- **Barbell row:** skipped — ended session early
**Strava data** ("Evening Weight Training", id 19715228649, includes cycle to/from gym): 98 min duration · 450 kcal · avg HR 98 bpm · max HR 152 bpm
**Coach review:**
- Squat progression today is genuinely good data — the 95×5 bridging set into a clean 100kg single with reserve left directly fixes the Aug 8 problem (previously jumped 90→100kg with no clean read). Confirms real strength gain, not just a grindy PR.
- Max HR (152) came in lower than Aug 8's 158 despite hitting the same top weight — consistent with today's single being controlled rather than a max-effort grind.
- Deadlift was capped by grip, not legs, across all sets — worth addressing directly. Recommended: lifting straps to keep testing leg/hip strength without grip as the bottleneck, plus dedicated grip work (farmer's carries, dead hangs) added into sessions to build it up independently.
- Barbell row skipped today — still the flagged laggard lift, pick up the 42.5kg target next leg day.
- **Recovery:** Heavy leg day — squat near-PR effort plus deadlift volume. Full rest tomorrow. Key signal isn't tonight's legs, it's tomorrow morning's first steps — this is potentially the second clean session (after Aug 8) that would open the door to reintroducing light calf/Achilles isolation work, pending how tomorrow morning feels.
